solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Bombshell not plain and dumb and, like, heartless? That's quite wrong

indicators.note: something quite wrong is badly out of order, so the gathered letters are to be rearranged
a heartless word loses its middle, leaving only its two outside letters

explanation.surface: A gushing put-down of a glamorous woman as dim, in teenage slang, is then rebuked as completely unfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' leaves LE from 'like'; the two 'and's just join the fodder words NOT, PLAIN and DUMB, which 'quite wrong' then rearranges with LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombshell is a strikingly attractive woman, and the classic Hollywood example had very pale hair.

clue.text: Post Office suggested ignoring first of letters? That's telling

indicators.note: ignoring the first of its letters tells us to drop the opening letter of the word for suggested

parts.note: suggested means hinted

explanation.surface: Someone notes the Post Office has hinted something while leaving out a letter, and calls that revealing.
explanation.definitionFit: A telling remark and a pointed one are both sharply significant, cutting home to the listener.

clue.text: Legislation amended after a complaint

indicators.note: amended means altered, so the letters of the following words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A law is changed in response to a grievance someone raised.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute passed by the UK Parliament is formally called by this name; legislation is the general term.

clue.text: Around start of Act I stab Shakespearean character

indicators.note: around here means turned round, so the two letters that follow are read backwards
the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a stab at something is a go, an attempt

explanation.surface: Stage directions: early in the first act, someone gets knifed.
explanation.definitionFit: The scheming ensign who destroys Othello is one of Shakespeare's best-known villains.

clue.text: Shunning exercise, superior rower produces row

indicators.note: shunning means avoiding, so those letters are removed from the word before

parts.note: superior means upper
PE is physical education, i.e. exercise
an oar is a rower, the person pulling one in a crew

explanation.surface: A top oarsman who skips training ends up causing a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A row, rhyming with cow, is a noisy disturbance or commotion, which is what an uproar is.

clue.text: Part of car in poor condition? Take in slope softly

indicators.note: take in means the outer word swallows the pieces that follow

parts.note: something in poor condition is bad
a rake is a slope, as of a theatre stage
p (piano) is the musical marking for softly

explanation.surface: A worn-out car part: ease it gently down the hill.
explanation.definitionFit: This friction component presses on the disc to slow a vehicle, and it is a common item in poor condition.

clue.text: Cartoon he'd redrawn, taking solid form

indicators.note: redrawn means sketched again differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist reworks a cartoon so it takes on three-dimensional shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight-faced polyhedron is a geometric solid, a solid form in the mathematical sense.

clue.text: Unsettled dance club, with doubt and blame flying about

parts.note: a disco is a dance club

indicators.note: letters flying about are scattered, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nightclub thrown into disarray as suspicion and accusations are tossed around.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsettled and confused or disconcerted: a jocular word for being thrown into mental disarray.

clue.text: Produce new version of expensive marque after first showing of Rolls

indicators.note: after puts the car's name behind that opening letter
the first showing of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the E-Type is the costly classic Jaguar sports car

explanation.surface: A luxury car maker produces a new model after the first Rolls appears.
explanation.definitionFit: To key a document in again is to make a fresh copy of it, a new version.

clue.text: A number curtailed urge enthralled by playwright with no little power

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive inside, so the shortened urge goes within the playwright
with no tells us to take the next letter out of the playwright

parts.note: Harold Pinter was an English playwright
P is the abbreviation for power

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, losing the last letter

parts.note: to urge someone on is to egg them on

explanation.surface: A curious account of an urge gripping a dramatist who has lost a little of his strength.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole number, positive, negative or zero, is a particular kind of number.

clue.text: It's time to interrupt live performer

indicators.note: to interrupt means to break into, so these letters go inside the word for live

parts.note: to live is to be, as in 'we are'
'tis is the old contraction of it is

explanation.surface: A cue to break into a live broadcast, because the moment has come.
explanation.definitionFit: An entertainer such as a singer or dancer is called by this term, especially in variety.

clue.text: Foodstuff that's a lot of use? Not a lot

indicators.note: not a lot of the phrase is used, just a few letters from inside it

explanation.surface: A wry question whether a food is very useful, answered with a dismissive no.
explanation.definitionFit: Bean curd made from soya milk is a staple food, especially in East Asian cooking.

clue.text: Mostly had geometry recast as a branch of applied mathematics

indicators.note: recast means formed again in a new mould, so the letters are reordered
mostly means all but the last letter

explanation.surface: A student's geometry homework is mostly reworked into a different subject.
explanation.definitionFit: The mathematical study of strategic decisions between competing players is a field of applied maths.

clue.text: With little hesitation, artist leading company among soldiers going to earth?

indicators.note: among means placed in the middle of, so these pieces go inside the soldiers

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, British reserve soldiers

indicators.note: leading puts the artist in front of the company

parts.note: er is a short hesitation sound
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
a firm is a company

explanation.surface: An artist heading a firm hesitates briefly while among troops digging in.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for solid ground, the phrase means dry land as opposed to sea or air: the earth underfoot.

clue.text: Block ears of college fellow about female, not male

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the college fellow goes round what follows

parts.note: a dean is a senior fellow of a college

indicators.note: not tells us to take the letters of the following word out of the one before

explanation.surface: A college fellow blocks a woman's hearing, but leaves the men alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone unable to hear, as loud noise does, is the effect of stopping up their ears.

clue.text: Part of bill? Chap lied unconvincingly about bill's first item

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the opening letter
lying unconvincingly garbles the story, so the letters are rearranged
the first item of a word is its initial letter

explanation.surface: A man fibs badly about the first line on an invoice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like an invoice; in the definition it is a bird's beak. 'unconvincingly' turns LIED into DILE, which goes about B.
explanation.definitionFit: Each half of a bird's beak is a mandible, so it is part of a bill in that sense.

clue.text: Scots commended, say, about party for disability supporter

parts.note: guid is the Scots word for good, what one says of something commended

indicators.note: about means going round, so the abbreviation surrounds the party

parts.note: eg (for example) is signalled by say
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Scottish praise, it seems, for a party held to support the disabled.
explanation.definitionFit: A trained dog leads a blind or partially sighted owner, supporting someone with a disability.

clue.text: Heath: "I governed, in retrospect, in a confused state"

indicators.note: in retrospect means looking back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: muir is the Scots word for moor or heath
governed means led

explanation.surface: Former PM Edward Heath looks back on his time in power and admits he was muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heath' tempts as Ted Heath, the former British prime minister; it is the Scots MUIR (moor).
explanation.definitionFit: A disturbed mental state with confusion and agitation, often from fever, is this condition.

clue.text: Early morning liquid to drink? It depends on the cow

parts.note: dew is the moisture found on grass early in the morning
to lap is to drink as a cat does

explanation.surface: Someone offers dew as a dawn drink, and says whether it is had depends on the cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depends' is used in its literal sense, hangs down.
explanation.definitionFit: The loose fold of skin hanging from a cow's throat is this, and depending literally means hanging down.

clue.text: Cut back one mammal or another

indicators.note: back means the word for cut is reversed

parts.note: to mow is to cut grass
a bat is a mammal

explanation.surface: A puzzling instruction to cut back one mammal or some other.
explanation.definitionFit: Another mammal: the burrowing Australian marsupial is a second example after the bat.

clue.text: Core part of stern audience not half doing for Roman playwright

indicators.note: the core part of a word is its middle, with the ends removed
not half means the first half of the word's letters is dropped

explanation.surface: The heart of a stern audience is not half won over by a classical dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Publius Terentius Afer was a comic dramatist of ancient Rome, known in English by this name.

clue.text: Confrontation about Liberal's trip overseas?

indicators.note: about means round, so the confrontation surrounds the party letter

parts.note: a fight is a confrontation
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A political row over a Liberal politician's foreign jaunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling abroad usually means an air journey, so a trip overseas is often one by plane.

clue.text: Supplied with booze beside shortened jetty in riverside area

indicators.note: beside places the drink phrase next to the cut jetty
shortened means losing the last letter

parts.note: a wharf is a jetty
supplied means fed
ale is booze

explanation.surface: Drinkers given beer next to a short pier somewhere by a river.
explanation.definitionFit: This valley of the River Wharfe in Yorkshire is a riverside area in northern England.

clue.text: Pop group curtailed promotional material

indicators.note: curtailed means docked, losing its last letter

parts.note: a blurb is the promotional text on a book jacket

explanation.surface: A band's publicity material is cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: This British band was one of the leading acts of the 1990s Britpop era, a pop group.

clue.text: Who's usually seriously shy, primarily?

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so the first letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A question asking who is the timid type, as a rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A weak, timid or ineffectual person is a slang term for someone usually rather shy.

clue.text: Claimed Bible was wrong

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
erred means was wrong

explanation.surface: Someone asserted the scriptures were mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to state firmly or assert, so the past tense means asserted or claimed.

clue.text: Stomach not repelled, swallowing last of meal? That's me!

indicators.note: swallowing means taking inside, so the stomach takes in the final letter

parts.note: the gut is the stomach

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter
repelled means driven back, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: A greedy eater whose stomach never rebels at the end of a meal owns up.
explanation.definitionFit: An overeater is exactly the person whose stomach swallows everything, so the clue speaks in that persona.

clue.text: This is a great ad for broadcasting — totally honest

indicators.note: broadcasting scatters something widely, so these letters are spread out and rearranged

explanation.surface: An advertiser boasts of a superb commercial ready to go on air, and swears it is truthful.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone completely honest and upright, like a true, unloaded die.
